sources.title: EffectConnect - Integrator platform voor Europese marketplaces
Top sports on marketplaces: the thriving success of Fitwinkel.nl
EffectConnect on the bol partner platform
Katapull breidt Commerce Hub uit met overname van Picqer
Vijf softwarebedrijven bundelen krachten in Katapull

items.title: Fixed subscription instead of revenue commission is a core differentiator
items.summary: EffectConnect publishes a Platform plan from EUR 305 per month (1,000 EANs, 500 orders, one marketplace, stock sync, feed manager with 5 exports, reporting, personal support), add-on modules from EUR 30 per month and a Scale plan on request. The bol partner listing states it charges no percentage of revenue and can be cancelled monthly; the Fitwinkel case cites a fixed fee per order as the reason to choose it.
items.implication: Pricing and metering bricks must make fixed-fee economics transparent; growth comes from add-ons and Scale upgrades rather than GMV share.

items.title: 50+ European marketplaces through one hub, with a strong bol heritage
items.summary: EffectConnect claims connections to 50+ European marketplaces (Amazon, bol, Decathlon, Kaufland, MediaMarkt, eBay, Kruidvat, Hornbach, Praxis and others), building marketplace integrations since 2012; bol lists it as a Gold Partner and as the first integrator to connect webshops to bol in 2011.
items.implication: The connector framework and channel-change absorption are the heart of the product; Benelux depth (bol LVB, Dutch support) is the moat versus global integrators.

items.title: Service-led onboarding is part of the product
items.summary: EffectConnect describes a four-step approach (get to know the business, bring data together, set up strategy, optimise and grow), a dedicated onboarding colleague, about two weeks to go live via app store or plugin, and a reported NPS of 67. Katapull positions the team configuring the setup with the merchant as a differentiator.
items.implication: Implementation tracking and account-health tooling for consultants deserve explicit bricks; time to go live is a load-bearing KPI.

items.title: Repricing is buy-box-centric and margin-bounded
items.summary: The repricer offers buy box strategies (compete only with fast or well-rated sellers, raise price stepwise when holding the buy box), a formula builder using purchase cost, commission and fixed costs, look-alike repricing, brand mode, grade matching for refurbished goods, min/max prices and a dedicated bol repricer per country. EffectConnect states about 98% of sales go through the buy box (its own claim).
items.implication: Pricing and repricing bricks separate formula calculation from competitive strategy and keep floors explicit.

items.title: Fulfilment Manager targets LVB and FBA sellers
items.summary: The Fulfilment Manager routes orders between own and marketplace warehouses by rules, prepares replenishments (warehouse assignment, split shipments, registration, labels), raises stock alarms and has an LVB switch that moves orders between Logistiek via bol and own stock; EffectConnect claims sellers can sell up to 14 times more often from own stock when marketplace stock runs out.
items.implication: Fulfilment routing and replenishment are distinct bricks next to stock sync; marketplace warehouse availability is a key operations KPI.

items.title: Content mapping and rules reduce listing rejections
items.summary: Content Mapping shows required attributes and allowed values per marketplace category and validates before go-live; Custom Attributes and smart data rules generate content; extra XML, CSV and Google Sheets feeds can be merged; automatic translations are available and multilingual catalogues are included. AI translation is sold as an add-on module.
items.implication: Catalogue, mapping, rule and translation bricks are separate so mappings can be reused across marketplaces and countries.

items.title: Embedded Integrations turn EffectConnect into a marketplace layer for other SaaS
items.summary: SaaS and logistics providers (WMS, TMS) can offer marketplace order and shipment connections inside their own platform via a Partner API (channels, connected channels, order retrieval, shipment updates) and branded authentication pages; the partner decides what to charge. DeliveryMatch, a Katapull sibling, is the named reference.
items.implication: A partner-tenant model, uniform order format and white-label UI are first-class bricks; this is the main bridge to sibling Katapull brands.

items.title: Katapull groups EffectConnect with back office, POS, logistics, EDI, returns and WMS brands
items.summary: Katapull (formed in 2025 from Logic4, DeliveryMatch, EffectConnect, Highbiza and Vendit; later adding Transus, Returnista and, in October 2026, Picqer) presents a Commerce Hub with 175+ specialists, 4,500+ customers in 40+ countries, 27,500+ users and 140+ marketplaces. EffectConnect's partner page lists DeliveryMatch, Highbiza, Logic4, Vendit, Transus and Returnista as Katapull partners.
items.implication: Hub-level identity, shared customer view and native connectors to sibling brands are strategic, but group figures are not EffectConnect figures.

items.title: Back-office vendors are retiring their own marketplace connectors in favour of the sister company
items.summary: In the Fitwinkel case, Logic4 phased out its own bol.com integration, after which Fitwinkel moved to EffectConnect and reports 20% revenue growth and 4-5 hours saved per week (company-reported case figures).
items.implication: Logic4/Vendit connectors are a key acquisition channel; migration from back-office-native connectors must be smooth.

items.title: Retail media reporting extends EffectConnect toward brands
items.summary: The Retail Media Dashboard, developed with OMG Transact, imports campaign data via retail media APIs of Amazon, bol and Albert Heijn (directly or via Criteo), allows manual entry for other retailers and compares performance and trade deals across retailers.
items.implication: A separate retail-media data asset and brick serve the brand persona; ROAS-style KPIs are modeled, not reported.

items.title: Consolidation among Dutch integrators raises switching opportunities
items.summary: ChannelEngine (Leiden) acquired Vendiro (Leiden, 70+ marketplaces) in June 2023; ChannelEngine reported 700+ channels then and now advertises 1,300+ channels.
items.implication: Merchants of acquired integrators re-evaluate; EffectConnect competes on Benelux depth, fixed pricing and Katapull back-office integration rather than channel count.
